newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moody's sees continued pressure on French banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's sees continued pressure on French banks.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday the outlook for French banks had not improved enough to remove medium-term pressure on their ratings as they enter a period of restructuring.
The rating agency said its current long-term deposit rating for French banks lies in the range of Aa3, down from Aa1 in the early 1990s. The average bank financial strength rating is C.

Moody's said in a statement that "selected rating adjustments are likely". It said it saw Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole and Societe Generale "as clearly emerging ... ahead of their domestic peers" from restructuring.

Summarising a new report on French banks, Moody's said "some of the largest institutions, Paribas, Indosuez, Credit Lyonnais, CIC and a number of second tier banks are emerging as weaker institutions and are prime targets for the coming phase of consolidation or restructuring".
The agency said the fact that regulators had failed to rescue several small specialised banks showed that existing support mechanisms were limited.
It also demonstrated the "possibility that investors and counterparties of small institutions could suffer losses".
The report says the bad-loan picture has brightened and that operating expenses are at least under control

But it adds: "Despite stronger revenues in 1995 and 1996, without major changes the French banks' earning power will continue being compromised by thin net interest margins, sluggish loan growth, the difficulty of boosting fee/commission income, and stubbornly expensive overheads."
